02: Edge Extraction - Finding the Important Edges

This lesson covers the first step of the pipeline: extracting edges from a mesh. We'll look at the actual algorithm used in generateEdges.js.

The Core Challenge

A mesh is just a list of triangles. Each triangle has 3 edges, but adjacent triangles share edges. We need to:

  1. Find which edges are shared between triangles
  2. Check if those shared edges meet our criteria (hard edge or silhouette)
  3. Handle boundary edges (edges with only one triangle)
Two adjacent triangles sharing an edge: A ─────────── B Triangle 1: A-B-C \ T1 / \ Triangle 2: B-D-C \ / \ \ / T2 \ Shared edge: B-C \ / \ C ───────── D When we process T1, we see edge B→C When we process T2, we see edge C→B (reversed!) We need to match these as the "same" edge.

The Algorithm Step-by-Step

1

Vertex Hashing

First, we convert each vertex position to a string "hash". This lets us compare vertices even when they have tiny floating-point differences. 

// Round to 4 decimal places (precision = 10000)
const precision = Math.pow(10, 4);  // = 10000

// Create hash for vertex at position (1.00001, 2.00002, 3.00003)
const hash = `${Math.round(x * precision)},${Math.round(y * precision)},${Math.round(z * precision)}`;
// Result: "10000,20000,30000"
2

Edge Hashing

We combine two vertex hashes to create an edge hash. The order matters - this lets us detect when two triangles share an edge (they'll have reversed hashes). 

// For triangle vertices A, B, C:
const hashA = "10000,0,0";
const hashB = "0,10000,0";
const hashC = "0,0,10000";

// Edge A→B
const edgeHash = `${hashA}_${hashB}`;      // "10000,0,0_0,10000,0"
const reverseHash = `${hashB}_${hashA}`;  // "0,10000,0_10000,0,0"

// If another triangle has edge B→A, its hash will match our reverseHash!
3

Building the Edge Map

As we iterate through triangles, we build a map of edges we've seen. When we encounter the reverse of an edge, we know we've found a shared edge. 

const edgeData = {};

// For each edge in the current triangle:
if (reverseHash in edgeData) {
    // Found the matching edge! Compare normals...
    const otherNormal = edgeData[reverseHash].normal;
    // ... check thresholds ...
    edgeData[reverseHash] = null;  // Mark as processed
} else if (!(hash in edgeData)) {
    // First time seeing this edge - store it
    edgeData[hash] = {
        index0: vertexIndex0,
        index1: vertexIndex1,
        normal: triangleNormal.clone()
    };
}
4

The Two Tests

When we find a matching edge, we perform two tests to decide if it should be drawn:

Test A: Hard Edge (Angle Threshold)
// thresholdAngle is in degrees (default: 50°)
const thresholdDot = Math.cos(thresholdAngle * Math.PI / 180);

// Compare the dot product of the two face normals
const meetsThreshold = normal1.dot(normal2) <= thresholdDot;

// If normals point in very different directions → hard edge!
// dot = 1: same direction (parallel faces)
// dot = 0: perpendicular (90° angle)
// dot = -1: opposite directions (180°)
Test B: Silhouette Edge (Projection Direction)
// projectionDirection is typically (0, 1, 0) for top-down view
let dot1 = projectionDirection.dot(normal1);
let dot2 = projectionDirection.dot(normal2);

// Handle nearly-vertical triangles (avoid floating point issues)
dot1 = Math.abs(dot1) < 1e-10 ? 0 : dot1;
dot2 = Math.abs(dot2) < 1e-10 ? 0 : dot2;

// If signs differ, one face is visible, one is hidden → silhouette!
const isSilhouette = Math.sign(dot1) !== Math.sign(dot2);
5

Handle Boundary Edges

After processing all triangles, some edges remain unmatched in our map. These are boundary edges - edges that belong to only one triangle (holes in the mesh, or non-manifold geometry). We always include these. 

// After the main loop, check for unmatched edges
for (const key in edgeData) {
    if (edgeData[key]) {  // Still has data (wasn't matched)
        // This is a boundary edge - add it to output
        const { index0, index1 } = edgeData[key];
        target.push(new Line3(v0, v1));
    }
}

Visual Example

Consider a simple "L" shape made of 2 quads (4 triangles): Top View: Side View (showing normals): ┌───────┬───────┐ N1↑ ↑N2 │ T1 │ T2 │ ┌─────┼─────┼─────┐ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ ├───────┼───────┤ Edge E │ │ E │ │ │ T3 │ T4 │ ─────► │ ↓ │ │ │ │ │ └─────┼─────┴─────┘ └───────┴───────┘ N3↓ Edge E is shared by T2 and T3. Test A (Angle): N2 · N3 = -1 (opposite directions) → cos(50°) ≈ 0.64 → -1 <= 0.64 ✓ HARD EDGE! Test B (Silhouette): Assuming top-down projection (0, 1, 0) → N2 · (0,1,0) > 0 (facing up) → N3 · (0,1,0) < 0 (facing down) → Signs differ ✓ SILHOUETTE EDGE! Result: Edge E is included in the output.

The Complete Flow

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ generateEdges() │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ INPUT: BufferGeometry with position attribute │ │ │ │ for each triangle (i = 0; i < indexCount; i += 3): │ │ │ │ │ ├─► Get vertices A, B, C │ │ ├─► Calculate triangle normal │ │ ├─► Create vertex hashes (4 decimal precision) │ │ ├─► Skip if degenerate (duplicate vertices) │ │ │ │ │ └─► for each edge (A→B, B→C, C→A): │ │ │ │ │ ├─► Create hash and reverseHash │ │ │ │ │ ├─► if reverseHash exists in edgeData: │ │ │ ├─► Get other triangle's normal │ │ │ ├─► Test A: dot(N1, N2) <= cos(threshold)? │ │ │ ├─► Test B: sign(proj·N1) ≠ sign(proj·N2)? │ │ │ ├─► if either test passes: ADD EDGE │ │ │ └─► Mark reverseHash as processed │ │ │ │ │ └─► else if hash not in edgeData: │ │ └─► Store edge with normal │ │ │ │ for each remaining unmatched edge in edgeData: │ │ └─► ADD EDGE (boundary edge) │ │ │ │ OUTPUT: Array of Line3 objects │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Key Points to Remember

Concept Purpose
Vertex Hashing (4 decimals) Handle floating-point imprecision when comparing positions
Edge Hash Direction Detect shared edges by looking for reversed hash
Angle Threshold Test Find hard edges where faces meet at sharp angles
Projection Direction Test Find silhouette edges where surface turns away
Boundary Edge Handling Include edges with only one adjacent triangle

Performance Note

The algorithm is O(n) where n is the number of triangles. Each triangle is visited once, and hash lookups are O(1). This is very efficient - even meshes with millions of triangles process quickly at this stage.

The iterationTime parameter allows the generator to yield periodically, keeping the UI responsive during processing.

src/utils/generateEdges.js
